NetCoreNOC shadow-mode report
==============================================================

A challenger runs beside the champion and writes its opinion where
nobody acts on it. THE BUILT-IN SCORER DECIDES EVERYTHING. There is no
promotion mechanism in this release, deliberately: a release that could
promote would be judged by the only metric it had, which would be
agreement with the champion.

-- SUFFICIENCY (read this first) -----------------------------
  verdict                                 SUFFICIENT

  floor                       required  observed
  split bags                        50        60
  mixed bags                        20        40
  merge-aware incidents             30       100
  distinct operators                 3         3
  top-operator share (max)       60.0%     34.0%

  ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS — not floors, and not substituted for one:
  split AND mixed bags      (no floor)        20
  asserted negative pairs     (server)         0
  client-reported marks       (client)         0
  `split AND mixed` is the population SECURITY-REVIEW-0.9.0 §5.4 argued
  the floor should be over — a `split` on a UNIFORM bag only says the
  champion should reject what it already rejects — and it floors NOTHING
  here: replacing a registered floor after seeing the data is what
  pre-registration prevents, so v0.10.0's plan decides it in advance.

  Every floor met. The floors were pre-registered before any result
  existed; a deployment may harden them and can never soften them.

-- the corpus ------------------------------------------------
  labelled bags (n)                          100
    confirm / split                      40 / 60
    MIXED (pairs both sides)                  40
  merge-aware incidents                      100
    one-hop count (superseded)               100
    reduction from one hop                     0
    unsound merge chains                       0
  pre-v0.8.0 merges (unrecoverable)            0
  distinct operators                           3
  promoted pairs behind them                 300
  label span (days)                        13.86
  legacy_capture rows included             False

  *n* IS BAGS, NOT PAIRS. Pairs from one alarm share a side; pairs from
  one situation are strongly correlated; two labels on situations that
  were merged are ONE incident. A MIXED bag is the only kind that
  contained a decision the champion could have got wrong.

  calibration at BAG level, Brier 0.005223
  bin              n    mean predicted    observed
  0.0-0.2         60            0.0828      0.0000
  0.2-0.4          0               n/a         n/a
  0.4-0.6          0               n/a         n/a
  0.6-0.8          0               n/a         n/a
  0.8-1.0         40            0.9472      1.0000

  CALIBRATION IS NOT IMPLIED BY ACCURACY. A model can rank perfectly and
  be badly calibrated, which is exactly where a threshold does the most
  damage. And the half that is a trap: CONFIDENCE MAY ROUTE WHAT THE
  OPERATOR IS ASKED; IT MAY NEVER AUTHORISE AUTONOMY. The autonomy
  trigger is measured agreement with humans, never a model's own
  certainty — a confidently wrong model is more dangerous than an
  uncertainly wrong one.

-- CHALLENGER, policy B: split discarded -----------------------
  intercept                             1.847774
  decay                                 1.671628
  class_affinity                        1.387365
  entity_affinity                       1.384296
  fingerprint                       e6867b5a474f
  training rows / bags                  120 / 40
  positive / negative mass          40.00 / 0.00
  training log loss (NOT quality)       0.004335

  >>> DEGENERATE: THIS POLICY DERIVED ONLY ONE CLASS. <<<
  With bag-level labels, discarding `split` discards the only source
  of negatives, so the target is constant and the best achievable
  model predicts 'link' unconditionally. The draft called policy B
  'throws away the minority class'; measured, it throws away the
  only class that could have taught anything. Reported rather than
  suppressed, because a policy whose failure is invisible is one a
  later release picks by default.

-- the admission filter --------------------------------------
                         median us      p99 us   terms   det   mem
  additive              <measured>  <measured>       3  True  True
  logistic-shadow       <measured>  <measured>       4  True  True

  admitted                    True

  THE CHAMPION IS MEASURED AGAINST THE SAME FILTER, on the same samples,
  in the same process. A filter nobody has run against the incumbent is a
  filter whose budget is a guess. The speed budget is a RATIO of the
  champion's p99, not a microsecond figure: Phase 0 measured the
  champion's own p99 moving 2.6x between two runs on one machine.

-- training/serving skew -------------------------------------
  sampled online opinions                      0
  challenger runs recorded                     1
  compared against reconstruction              0
  unmatched (no captured pair)                 0
  DIVERGED                                     0
  divergence rate                           n/a%

  THE TWO MECHANISMS ARE NOT ALTERNATIVES. Offline reconstruction
  measures quality at no ingest cost and CANNOT measure skew by
  construction — recomputing from the stored features is tautologically
  consistent with them. Online shadow measures real latency and real
  behaviour and says nothing further about quality. THEIR DIVERGENCE IS
  THE TEST, compared with == on the float rather than a tolerance.
  The pre-registered expectation is 0.0000%. Any non-zero rate is a
  DEFECT, and it means the quality figures above describe features that
  were never served.

-- what this report CANNOT tell you --------------------------
  * whether the challenger should be promoted. There is no promotion
    mechanism here and no evaluator worth trusting yet; that is v0.10.0
    and v0.11.0, in that order and for that reason.
  * whether either scorer is RIGHT. The truth here is what an operator
    said about a grouping they were shown, at bag granularity.
  * anything from a pairwise accuracy. The champion accepts 99.83% of
    evaluated pairs, so a constant 'link' scores 99.83%. No pairwise
    accuracy is reported anywhere above, deliberately.
  * how a model would behave on a different network. The held-out split
    this release uses is a reporting device over an n in the tens, and
    it is NOT v0.10.0's split.
